about: Representative real-provider evaluation set. Cases run in the order of `order` so that, if the budget runs out, the least important cases are the ones skipped.

generations.prompt: A todo app: customers call an API gateway; an orders service handles requests and persists to PostgreSQL.
A checkout flow: customers hit an API gateway routed to an order service which charges Stripe.
A catalog app: customers call an API gateway; a catalog service serves items from PostgreSQL.

A video streaming platform: viewers use web and TV apps through a CDN; an API gateway routes to catalog, playback and recommendation services; playback writes view events to Kafka, consumed by an analytics service that stores aggregates in ClickHouse; user accounts live in PostgreSQL and sessions in Redis.

Riders and drivers use mobile apps that talk to an API over WebSockets for live location. A matching service pairs riders with nearby drivers using a geospatial index in Redis; trips are stored in PostgreSQL; payments go through Stripe; push notifications go through Firebase.
A blog.

An internal HR tool: employees sign in with Okta SSO and submit leave requests through a React app to a Django backend, which stores data in MySQL and emails managers through SendGrid. A nightly Celery job syncs leave balances to Workday.

Thousands of temperature sensors publish readings over MQTT to a broker; an ingestion service validates them and writes to TimescaleDB; an alerting service watches thresholds and pages on-call engineers through PagerDuty; a Grafana dashboard reads from TimescaleDB.

Shoppers search products in a Next.js storefront; a search service queries Elasticsearch, which is kept in sync with the product database (PostgreSQL) by a change-data-capture pipeline using Debezium and Kafka.

A fraud-detection system: the payments service sends each transaction to a scoring service that loads a model from S3 and features from a Redis feature store, returns a risk score, and logs decisions to BigQuery for retraining in a weekly Airflow pipeline.
A user logs in with email and password: the web app calls the auth service, which checks the password hash in PostgreSQL and issues a JWT; the web app stores the token and loads the dashboard.

Checkout: the customer submits an order; the order service reserves stock with the inventory service and charges the card through Stripe. If payment fails it releases the reserved stock and returns an error; on success it publishes an OrderPlaced event.

Password reset: the user requests a reset link; the account service generates a one-time token, stores it in Redis with a 15-minute expiry and emails the link through SES. When the user opens the link, the token is verified and deleted.
File upload: the browser asks the API for a pre-signed S3 URL, uploads the file directly to S3, then notifies the API, which enqueues a virus scan; the scanner marks the file clean or quarantined.
Data model for a library: books have many copies; members borrow copies through loans with due dates; a loan belongs to one member and one copy; members can reserve books.
Data model for a multi-tenant project tracker: organizations have users and projects; projects have tasks; each task has an assignee (a user), comments, and labels (many-to-many).
Data model for an online course platform: instructors create courses with ordered lessons; students enroll in courses; each enrollment tracks progress per lesson and a final certificate.

Component detail of an order service: an HTTP controller, an order application service, a pricing component, an order repository backed by PostgreSQL, and an outbox publisher that sends events to Kafka.

Component detail of a notification service: a queue consumer reads notification requests, a template renderer builds messages, a channel router picks email, SMS or push, and adapters call SendGrid, Twilio and Firebase; delivery results are stored in DynamoDB.

Component detail of an authentication service: login and token endpoints, a password verifier using bcrypt, a token issuer that signs JWTs with keys from a KMS, a refresh-token store in Redis, and an audit logger that writes to Kafka.

refinements.instruction: Add a Redis cache that the orders service reads from.
Add a notification service that emails the customer a receipt after the order service charges Stripe.
Rename the matching service to Dispatch Service.
The nightly job should also export a CSV report to an S3 bucket.
Put the catalog service and PostgreSQL inside a Catalog domain boundary.
